geometry.note: OpenStreetMap footprint alone (itself taken from King County GIS), with the building identified by an official CENPA page; confidence capped at approximate by the OSM rank. CENPA's '53,500-sq. ft.' is a floor area, not a footprint, so it is not used as a check: the 3833 m2 footprint is 41 260 sq ft and the OSM two levels would give about 82 500 sq ft, the official figure lying between them.
geometry.quote: CENPA is located at the North Physics Lab: a 53,500-sq. ft. stand-alone facility

method: OpenStreetMap building way 885743335, name 'North Physics Laboratory', ref 'NPV', house number 4311 on Pend Oreille Road Northeast (building:levels=2, start_date 1963, source King County GIS), used verbatim. CENPA's own About page says CENPA 'is located at the North Physics Lab'; the house number 4311 matches the laboratory's published address and its contact page directs visitors down Pend Oreille Rd.
name: North Physics Laboratory, home of CENPA (University of Washington)
notes: The CENPA page gives its shipping address as 4311 Mason Place NE while OSM files the building under 4311 Pend Oreille Road NE; the house number is the same and Pend Oreille Rd is the access road the contact page names. The existing site point (47.659385, -122.302645) is a Nominatim hit on the Mason Place address and lies about 80 m south of this building's centroid.

summary.plain: The North Physics Laboratory building on the University of Washington campus in Seattle, which houses CENPA and the ADMX axion experiment.
